BLOOD LOSS Blood loss, as in the event of gastric ulceration
or dysmenorrhea (abnormal menses) can deplete the body of 
signiﬁ cant amounts of iron. Blood losses require homeostatic
restoration of blood volume.50 If volume is restored, but new 
RBC have not been produced at the same rate, the number of 
viable RBC in a given volume of blood is decreased; this results 
in a functional anemia, a situation where oxygen is insuﬃ  cient
due to inability to transport the appropriate amount needed for 
function. In the event that erythropoiesis cannot keep up with 
RBC losses, depletion of iron stores in the liver, spleen, and oth-
er tissues results. Depletion of iron from ferritin, hemosiderin 
(another storage form of iron), or transferrin can be measured 
to ascertain the extent of the depletion. Th ese levels are closely 
tied to total iron available to the body for use.
INADEQUATE INTAKE AND/OR ABSORPTION Iron

conjunction with greater needs, as with a vegan female who is
